base_candidates_ranked.reason: The larger discovery cohort (364 cases) used data-independent acquisition (DIA) with a spectral library approach (Prosit/ScaffoldDIA) and label-free quantification (normalized intensities).
The smaller discovery cohort (59 cases) used data-dependent acquisition (DDA) and label-free quantification (iBAQ).

workflow: Mass spectrometry was performed with data-dependent acquisition (DDA) for the 59 case cohort and with data-independent acquisition (DIA) from the 364 case cohort.
Normalized iBAQ values from MaxQuant were used for quantitation.
ScaffoldDIA (Proteome software) was used to configure DIA library searches.
differential: To consider a protein as a potential new target antigen, we looked for outlier proteins in the mass spectrometry data that were enriched in unknown membranous samples as compared with control samples of known antigen types.
For all new target antigens, peptides showed orders of magnitude higher intensity in the index cases (on a log2 scale) compared to control cases.
For statistical hypothesis testing, a two-sample t-test was performed for each protein using normalized iBAQ values for the two groups.
search_parameters: Proteins digestion was performed using sequencing-grade trypsin
Immunoprecipitations were performed through addition of 50 µl of magnetic protein G Dynabeads
